headline: Wall Street Logs a Winning Week as Healthcare and Software Lead Friday's Advance
body_html:
Markets closed out a constructive Friday session on October 9, with 344 stocks rising against 196 declining across our 544-name universe. Healthcare topped the sector leaderboard, gaining 1.45%, while Software added 1.04%. Materials, Industrials, and Energy posted modest advances. Consumer names were effectively flat, whereas Semiconductors slipped 0.48% and Homebuilders bore the sharpest pressure, down 1.44% on the day.

The session's standout move came from Hims & Hers Health, which surged 10.19%, anchoring a strong showing across telehealth and life-sciences tools. Cybersecurity and data-platform software names also charged higher, with Zscaler up 7.80%, Snowflake climbing 7.42%, and Datadog advancing 7.11%. On the downside, audio-chip maker Cirrus Logic and RF specialist Skyworks Solutions each shed more than 5%, dragging on the broader semiconductor group. Real-estate brokerage eXp World Holdings led all decliners, falling 7.23%.

Wall Street heads into the new week carrying those gains, with earnings season accelerating and a fresh round of inflation data on the calendar. Geopolitical risk has risen sharply after Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia's Riyadh airport killed twelve people — the deadliest attack on the kingdom in a decade — rattling Gulf markets and sending oil prices higher. Traders return Monday, October 12, with that backdrop squarely in focus.

briefs.headline: Houthi Assault on Riyadh Airport Marks Deadliest Strike on Saudi Arabia in Years
briefs.body: A drone or missile attack on Riyadh's main airport killed twelve people, making it the most lethal strike against the kingdom in roughly a decade. Yemen's Houthi movement has since warned airlines and travelers to avoid Saudi airports, injecting fresh uncertainty into Gulf aviation and regional commerce.

briefs.headline: Major Saudi Business Conferences Press On Despite Airport Violence
briefs.body: Organizers of high-profile Saudi Arabia conferences confirmed their events would proceed as scheduled following the deadly airport strike. The signal of continuity is being closely watched as a gauge of investor and corporate confidence in the kingdom's stability amid an escalating Houthi campaign.

briefs.headline: U.S. Military Intercepts Cargo Vessel Attempting to Break Iran Blockade
briefs.body: American forces disabled a cargo ship that sought to breach the U.S.-enforced blockade of Iran, marking one of the more direct naval confrontations in recent months. The incident adds another layer of tension to Middle East shipping lanes already strained by the Houthi threat to Saudi ports.

briefs.headline: Oil Settles Higher as Hurricane Threat Curbs Gulf of Mexico Output
briefs.body: Crude prices ended the week on a firmer note after producers preemptively shut in production ahead of an approaching hurricane. Supply disruptions in the Gulf of Mexico, layered on top of Middle East instability, gave energy markets added support heading into the new trading week.

briefs.headline: AI-Driven Volatility Defined Last Week's Swings Across Growth Names
briefs.body: Technology stocks swung sharply in both directions last week as investors continued to reassess valuations tied to artificial-intelligence spending. The turbulence underscored how sensitive growth-oriented positions remain to shifts in sentiment, even as several software and security names finished Friday strongly in the green.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court Weighs Landmark 401(k) Case Over Private-Fund Exposure
briefs.body: The nation's highest court is weighing a significant retirement-plan case that could reshape how fiduciaries select and retain private funds inside 401(k) plans. The justices' preliminary leanings suggest a close decision, with potential consequences for plan sponsors and asset managers across the industry.
